transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom Enterprise Support. My name is Alex. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hello, Alex. My name is Sandra Smith with Velocity Transportation. I'm having a really frustrating issue with my mobile service.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry to hear you're experiencing frustration, Sandra. I can definitely look into that for you. To access your account, could you please provide your Customer ID?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it's CUST-2014.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. That's CUST-2014. And for security, could you please verify the 6-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let me see... yes, it's 168985.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, that matches. Thank you for verifying your information, Sandra. I have your account for Velocity Transportation pulled up now. How can I assist with your mobile service today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Well, I keep dropping calls. It's happening constantly. I work from a home office, and the reception down in my basement office is just terrible. Every time I take a business call, it cuts out or drops completely. It's unprofessional and it's affecting my work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how disruptive that would be. Dropped calls are definitely not the experience we want for our customers, especially when you're trying to run a business. Let's see what we can do to get this sorted out for you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I hope so. It's getting to be a real problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm going to start by checking the network coverage in your area. Can you please confirm the full physical address where you're experiencing these issues?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure, it's 123 Industrial Way, Suite B, in Boulder, Colorado, 80301.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. 123 Industrial Way, Suite B. And what is the make and model of the phone you're using?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It's an iPhone 14 Pro.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, great. Please give me about 30 to 45 seconds while I analyze the signal data from the cell towers near your location. I'm going to check for any reported outages or known signal degradation. Do you mind holding for a moment?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's fine. Go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience, Sandra. I've reviewed the network map and performance logs for your area.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The good news is there are no outages, and the outdoor signal strength from the nearest Cymbal Telecom tower is very strong. However, what you're describing is a classic case of signal attenuation.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Signal what?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Attenuation. It basically means the signal gets weaker as it passes through physical barriers. Since your office is in a basement, the radio waves have to travel through the ground, concrete foundations, and other building materials, which significantly weakens them before they can reach your phone.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So... I'm just stuck with bad service in my office forever? That's not going to work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all. There is an excellent solution for this exact scenario. I see on your account that you have our Enterprise Dedicated Ethernet service, which means you have a very strong and stable Wi-Fi signal in your building, correct?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, the Wi-Fi is fantastic. Never have a problem with it. It's the 'Cymbal Wi-Fi' network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. We can use that strong Wi-Fi connection to solve your mobile call problem by enabling a feature called Wi-Fi Calling.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Wi-Fi Calling? What's that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It allows your phone to make and receive calls and texts over a Wi-Fi network instead of the cellular network. When your phone is connected to your 'Cymbal Wi-Fi', it will automatically route calls through your internet connection. The quality is crystal clear, and it completely bypasses the weak cellular signal in your basement.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, wow. I didn't know that was possible. And it uses my same phone number?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. Everything works exactly the same. Same number, same contacts, same call log. Your phone just intelligently switches to the best available network, which in your basement, is Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, that sounds like exactly what I need. How do I turn it on?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can walk you through it right now. It only takes a couple of minutes. Do you have your iPhone with you?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I'm holding it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. First, please open the 'Settings' app. It's the icon that looks like a gear.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, I'm in Settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, scroll down a bit and tap on 'Phone'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hmm, I don't see 'Phone'. I see 'Cellular'...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My apologies, you're right. On some newer iOS versions the path has changed. Please tap on 'Cellular'.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, tapped 'Cellular'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In that menu, do you see an option that says 'Wi-Fi Calling'?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, I see it. It says 'Off'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Please tap on that.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now you should see a toggle switch for 'Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone'. Please slide that to the on position.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Done. A pop-up just appeared. It says 'Enable Wi-Fi Calling?' and has a lot of text about location and emergency calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's a very important step. Please tap the 'Enable' button.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, enabled. Now it's asking me to update my emergency address.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct. This is crucial. When you call 911 from a regular cell signal, they can triangulate your location. With Wi-Fi Calling, they can't, so we need to provide your physical address so emergency services can find you if you ever need them.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That makes sense. So I should put in my office address here?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, please enter the 123 Industrial Way address, including Suite B, and confirm it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, typing it in... 123 Industrial Way... Suite B... Boulder... Colorado... 80301. Okay, I've entered it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there a 'Save' or 'Confirm' button?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, it says 'I agree to the terms and conditions'. I'll check that and hit continue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, it says 'Your emergency address has been updated'. And now I'm back on the Wi-Fi Calling screen, and the toggle is green, it's on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic. You've successfully enabled it. Now for the final confirmation. If you look at the very top left of your iPhone's screen, next to the Wi-Fi symbol, what does it say?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It says... 'Cymbal Wi-Fi'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's exactly what we want to see. That text confirms your phone is now primed to make and receive calls over your Wi-Fi network. The cellular signal bars are now irrelevant as long as you're connected to Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So, in theory, my problem is solved?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In theory, yes. But I'd like to prove it to you with a quick test, if you have another minute.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Of course. What do I need to do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I need you to stay exactly where you are, in the basement office where the signal is normally bad. In a moment, I'm going to ask you to hang up this call.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As soon as you hang up, I am going to call you right back on this same number. Answer the call, and we can confirm the call quality. This will prove that incoming calls are now working perfectly over Wi-Fi.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sounds like a plan. I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. Please hang up now, and I will call you back immediately.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, hanging up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello again, Sandra. Did the call come through?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes! It rang right away. And wow... you sound perfectly clear. There's no static or cutting out at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful news. That's the quality you can expect from now on when you're in your office. That call was made entirely over your Cymbal Wi-Fi network.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is a huge relief. I can't tell you how much of a headache this has been.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm very glad we could get it resolved so easily for you. We've confirmed incoming calls work. To be thorough, do you have a moment to test an outgoing call?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sure. How do I do that while I'm on the phone with you?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can just call a colleague or even your own voicemail. The important thing is to initiate the call from your end while you're in the basement and see if it connects clearly.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay. Can you hold on for a minute? I'll call my main office line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. I'll stay on the line. Take your time.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, Alex, are you still there?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I'm here.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It worked! It connected instantly, and the automated attendant on our main line was perfectly clear. No issues at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. That confirms it. Both incoming and outgoing calls are now working flawlessly over Wi-Fi. Your dropped call issue in the basement office is officially resolved.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: This is fantastic. Thank you so much, Alex. I feel like I should have called months ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. I'm just happy we could provide a simple and effective solution for you today. Just remember, this will work on any trusted Wi-Fi network you connect to, so if you're ever in another location with poor cell service but good Wi-Fi, your phone will automatically use it.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's even better. So this setting is permanent, I don't need to do this again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct, it's a one-time setup. It will remain active unless you manually turn it off in your phone's settings.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I won't be doing that! This is great.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've also added detailed notes to your account, CUST-2014, documenting the issue and the resolution by enabling Wi-Fi Calling. This way, if any of your colleagues at Velocity Transportation have a similar issue, any agent who helps them can see this solution worked for you.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's very thoughtful, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are most welcome. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, Sandra? Any other questions about your Cymbal Telecom services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that was the only thing, but it was a big thing. You've solved my problem completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm delighted to hear that. For your records, the reference number for this call is 7741-098. Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom Enterprise Support, and have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too, Alex. Thanks again. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, call ended. Adding final notes. Issue: Poor cellular reception in basement office causing dropped calls. Resolution: Guided customer to enable Wi-Fi Calling on iPhone 14 Pro. Tested incoming and outgoing calls successfully. Customer confirmed issue is resolved. Closing ticket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me just double check the E911 address entry. Yes, 123 Industrial Way, Suite B. All good.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The corporate account profile looks good. Velocity Transportation, CUST-2014. All services active, account in good standing. No other open tickets.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: This is a common one. A lot of customers aren't aware of Wi-Fi calling. It's a great first-line fix before discussing expensive signal boosters.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, notes are saved, ticket is closed. Ready for the next call.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's see... Next call in queue. Okay, let's go.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright, final check on my after-call work for Sandra Smith. Everything is documented. Call reference 7741-098. All set.
